elements.element: If renewal is non-automatic, renewal may occur only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because both the Agreement and Attachment use automatic renewal. The automatic-renewal alternative is therefore the operative preferred pathway.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be twelve (12) months.
elements.evidence: Both the Agreement and Attachment automatically renew for periods of twelve (12) months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to opt out by giving thirty (30) days’ notice before renewal.
elements.evidence: Both provisions allow either party, which includes Customer, to prevent renewal by giving thirty (30) days’ written notice before the end of the then-current period.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer of each upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Both provisions require MSL to notify IBM of each upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current period, supplying the required Vendor-to-Customer reminder.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent (3%).
elements.evidence: Both provisions cap any renewal-period price increase at the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve months or three percent (3%).

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, the non-renewal notice window must be no more than sixty (60) days.
elements.evidence: Both automatic-renewal provisions use a thirty (30)-day notice window, which is no more than sixty days.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed five percent (5%).
elements.evidence: Both provisions impose the stricter cap of the lesser of CPI and three percent (3%), necessarily remaining at or below five percent.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the automatic-renewal branch of the preferred position for both the Agreement and Attachment and therefore also exceeds the fallback. The changes are confined to renewal duration, notice timing, reminders, price caps, and a necessary Attachment-specific reference. Unrelated initial-term and termination provisions remain effective. Drafting is strong, though the applicable CPI index could be identified more precisely.
